source: due2-native: a constraint on the party that a DPROD duty's dprod:subjectOfDuty names (#129)
notes: Not valid ODRL 2.2: odrl:constraint has the domain Policy or Rule (Vocabulary §3.14.2), and ex:alice is a Party, since dprod:subjectOfDuty is rdfs:subPropertyOf odrl:function, whose range is odrl:Party. Both checkers test the domain itself rather than a list of the nodes a constraint may not sit on, so a node that a profile's own party role reaches is covered.

expected_rejection.why: ex:alice, the bearer that ex:report's dprod:subjectOfDuty names, carries an odrl:constraint, and the ODRL vocabulary places a constraint only on a Policy or a Rule (Vocabulary §3.14.2). Normalisation rejects a constraint outside its place in stage 1 (odrl-compound-to-atomic-normalization.md §3), so W1 rejects the policy.
